articleTitle: A Wearable Filtering Antenna Based on Multilayer Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact wearable filtering antenna based on multilayer structure is proposed for modern wireless communication systems. Different dielectric materials are selected to satisfy the design requirements. The filtering antenna system consists of two λ/2 hairpin resonators which improve the selectivity of passband and a rectangular patch antenna which also works as the last order resonator of the filter structure. Comparing with antenna structure, a harder and smaller dielectric slab used for filtering network can reduce the performance deterioration caused by the deformation of the textile material where the antenna is located. The simulated results shows that the filter-antenna features 12.2% bandwidth for f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> = 5.5GHz with peak radiation gain of -5.4dB.

articleTitle: Transmission Error Correction Using Eigenvectors in MIMO Radar with Overlapping Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the MIMO radar using the transmission antenna switching, the phase and amplitude errors in the transmission signals may yield deterioration of the estimation accuracy of target directions. In this paper, we introduce overlapping elements in the virtual array of MIMO radar, and we improve the estimation accuracy by correcting transmission signal errors with the eigenvectors of receive correlation matrix.

articleTitle: Wideband RCS Reduction Based on Dual-Polarization Frequency Selective Rasorber
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a kind of frequency selective rasorber. By combining the upper lossy layer and the bottom lossless layer, one passband with two-sided absorption band is obtained. A 4×4 array is constructed to realize radar cross section (RCS) reduction.The 5dB RCS redction bandwidth is from 5GHz to 15GHz(relative bandwidth is 100%). It is also worth pointing out that the maximum RCSR is 29.7dB and 31.2dB around 8.8GHz for x- and y-polarized incident waves.

articleTitle: Dual Polarization 4x4 MIMO Sub-6GHz Multi-Beam Base Station Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of compact dual polarized 4x4 MIMO sub-6GHz multi-beam base station antennas covering frequencies from 3.3 to 3.8 GHz. The 4x4 MIMO multi-beam antennas are realized through stacking two 2x2 MIMO multi-beam antenna arrays vertically. By using different numbers of columns and rows of the antenna array, the several 4x4 MIMO 3-beam and 6-beam antennas are designed and tested. Detailed array architecture and corresponding measured results are presented.

articleTitle: A Study of Impedance Switched Folded Monopole Antenna with Robustness to Metal
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to achieve an antenna with robustness to metal for closed space wireless communications, the impedance characteristics of folded monopole antennas (FMA) have been investigated in detail. In this study, we propose the folded monopole antenna, which can switch the input impedance and resonant frequency by a simple method. Simulated results show the antenna which can be switched to three modes with different resonant frequencies and input impedance by controlling the connection of the antenna elements.

articleTitle: Modeling of Corroded Reinforcing Bar for Nondestructive Inspection of Concrete Using UWB Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an analysis model of corroded rebar for nondestructive inspection (NDI) of concrete structures using ultra-wideband (UWB) radar and shows some simulation results. Corrosion is modeled by a rust layer formed by rusting of rebar surface and a transition layer between the rust layer and surrounding healthy concrete. Distribution of complex permittivity in transition layer is determined by solving a diffusion equation of rust particle. UWB radar responses from some different corroded samples are shown as simulation results.

articleTitle: Compact Antenna Using Novel Finger-Connected Interdigital Capacitor-Based Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavity
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A electrical small antenna using a novel finger-connected interdigital capacitor (FC-IDC), based on composite right/left handed (CRLH) unit cell, is proposed in this paper. The proposed CRLH antenna consists of a thin rectangle substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity with the etched interdigital slot on the top metal surface and two etched slot rings on the bottom metal surface, which is fed by a grounded co-planar waveguide (GCPW). The interdigital slot acts as a series capacitor as well as a radiator leading to a CRLH antenna application. Compared to other conventional CRLH antenna, the proposed one has a lower -1st-order resonant mode. thus, the present design has a smaller electrical size. The results show that the antenna using a novel CRLH-TL unit cell based on FC-IDC achieves 30.5% reductions in operating frequencies compared with the conventional CRLH antennas with the same size. In addition, the novel designed antenna can be easily fabricated by printed circuit board technology, which is of important significance in the miniaturization of communication system.

articleTitle: Analysis of Satellite-ground Frequency Deviation and Compensation Method for LEO Mobile Communication System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Due to the shortage of spectrum resource and fierce competition of LEO mobile communication system, improving the efficiency of spectrum resource utilization becomes critical to system design. In LEO mobile communication system, user-segment uplink is the key to the entire system, and the improvement of spectrum resource utilization in user-segment uplink can significantly improve the spectral efficiency of the entire system. Based on the technical characteristics of typical LEO mobile communication systems in the world, this paper analyses the mechanism of frequency deviation between satellite and ground of LEO mobile communication system, and gives the corresponding compensation method for frequency deviation. Our method reduces the protection bandwidth of user-segment uplink, which further improves the efficiency of spectrum resource utilization.

articleTitle: Study of Mutual Coupling Reduction for PIFA MIMO Antenna with Pattern Diversity for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, three different methods of spatial and pattern diversity have been studied to reduce mutual coupling and improve the overall performance of a PIFA MIMO. The proposed antenna consists of parasitic wall elements embedded at the edge of the ground plane with U-slot in the middle of the ground plane is fabricated using copper sheet with thickness of 0.45 mm and air as the dielectric substrates. The performance of the proposed antenna is simulated using CST Microwave Studio Software. The proposed antenna is measured to validate the simulation results. The best isolation of greater than 20 dB were achieved in the both simulated and measured antenna. Thus this proposed PIFA MIMO offers a promising solution for future 5G wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: An Efficient Wideband Analysis Method Based on ASED Basis Function Method and Improved FIR For Large-Scale Finite Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An efficient wideband analysis method for the large-scale finite periodic structures is presented by using the accurate sub-entire domain (ASED) basis function method and the improved frequency-independent reaction (FIR). By using the ASED basis function, the number of unknowns can be reduced from QN<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> to N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, where Q is the number of Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions defined on each cell and N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> is the number of cells. By using the improved FIR for frequency sweep, the impedance matrix elements can be efficiently computed. In this method, the impedance elements are classified as two categories: near-region ones and far-region ones. The former ones are computed by using the method based on the Taylor series expansion. The latter ones are calculated using the technique based on the equivalent dipole-moment method. Several examples are conducted in order to demonstrate the proposed technique. Simulation results show that good agreement between the results of the proposed technique and the results of the ASED-FIR is achieved. The CPU time can be reduced by almost 40% comparing with the ASED-FIR.

articleTitle: A comb-like dipole array with wide bandwith and scanning properties
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present a comb-like connected dipole array with integrated Marchand balun, which contain strip-line, dipole and vertical metal strips. The vertical metal strips located at the edges of the element to connect the dipole and ground, also serve as ground for Marchand. In this way, we can avoid the appearance of any resonant common-mode in the working band. What's more, an even current distributions on the dipoles can be achieved, which will be enhanced to stabilize the performance of array at different scanning angle. the proposed approach provides 4.58:1 bandwidth with VSWR <; 2.2 throughout the entire scanning range of ±60° in E plane without any superstrate.

articleTitle: Design of a non-uniform 8-element array for passive coherent location systems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a non-uniform 8-element array antenna to maximize the beamforming performance of FM based PCL systems. The proposed non-uniform array has two elements groups with different distances from the center to element. Beamforming performances such as PSLR and HPBW are compare with a uniform circular array, and the result demonstrates that the proposed non-uniform array has a HPBW narrower than a uniform circular array while maintaining a high PSLR.

articleTitle: Design of Microwave Radiating SIW Diplexer
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a new design for the integration of microwave SIW diplexer and antenna using multilayer planar technology. The design process started with the network synthesis of the SIW diplexer integrated with patch antenna using lumped lowpass prototype networks. The circular cavity structure using TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</sub> mode is employed in the design of the diplexer and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</sub> mode for the antenna. To prove the design concept, modes in the SIW diplexer and in the microstrip antenna are coupled by capacitive circular aperture at the common ground plane. The proposed design is fabricated with standard printed circuit board technology and will be operating at 2.2 GHz and 2.4 GHz each suitable for LTE/WiFi applications. The performance of the proposed design are verified through both simulation and measurement. The measured results showed a good agreement with passband return loss greater than 10 dB in both bands and 20 MHz bandwidth with good radiation pattern and radiation gain measured to be 5.55 dBi and 5.84 dBi.

articleTitle: Multiband UWB Antenna for On-Body Wireless Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Wireless Body Area Networks (WBAs an emerging technology due to its many possible applications in the society especially in the field of health monitoring. With the increase of communications standards utilizing the Ultra Wide Band (UWB), there tends to be interference on WBAN applications. In this work, a multiband antenna was implemented covering frequencies from 5.9 - 6.6 GHz and 8.45 - 9.25 GHz to minimize the interference caused by known standards. The designed antenna was able to achieve an S11 of less than -10 dB at the operating frequencies. It was also determined that placing a distance of at least 10mm between the designed antenna and human body phantom would substantially remove the degradation caused by the human body. The designed antenna is able to isolate the defined interferences by using multiple bands and allows more efficient usage of the UWB for on-body wireless body area networks.

articleTitle: Amplitude and Phase Controllable Transmissive Coding Metasurface for Arbitrary Wavefront Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Coding metasurafces have enjoyed an overwhelming development in recent years due to their digital properties in controlling electromagnetic (EM) waves. In this paper, we propose a novel type of amplitude and phase controllable transmissive coding metasurface, in which the patches and slots are integrated together in the unique coding particle, implying to manipulate the amplitude and phase responses independently and simultaneously. We select the coding particles with 1-bit phase states and continual amplitude states to tailor the EM wavefront arbitrarily, such as sinusoidal and sinc-function profiles. The excellent results indicate the strong EM manipulating ability in actual applications.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Antenna Array using Integrated Butler Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-beam antenna array using integrated butler feeding network is proposed for radio frequency (RF)-complexity reduction. The proposed antenna array consists of eight identical dipole antenna elements, which are fed with Γ-like structure. The integrated butler feeding network is laid out to form a special phase distribution that can achieve dual-beam in the vertical dimension. Compared with the traditional antenna array, only a quarter of ports are employed to excite all antenna elements in the proposed array, which can reduce RF-complexity enormously. The simulated results show that the main beams at +21° and -21° in E-plane and the gain of 10.4 dBi are achieved at 2.6 GHz.

articleTitle: A K/Ka Multi-Polarized Dielectric Rod Antenna Based on A Wideband Band OMT
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband multi-polarized dielectric rod antenna is proposed. By employing the orthomode transducer (OMT) feeding structure which is realized by using ridged waveguides, the impedance bandwidth of the antenna is widened effectively and the multi-polarized radiation performance is achieved. The antenna can be operated in dual polarization in the frequency range of 21-34 GHz, while operated in circularly polarization (AR <; 3 dB) in the frequency range of 29.9-30.2 GHz. The antenna can be used in satellite and 5G communications.

articleTitle: A Novel Compact Printed Monopole Antenna with Folded-Line SIR Loading
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact printed monopole antenna with a folded-line stepped impedance resonator (SIR) is presented. By loading a folded-line SIR with internal coupling at the bottom of the printed monopole antenna, a compact antenna can be achieved. The resonant frequency is reduced by the strong coupling between the folded-line SIR and the printed monopole. The size of the antenna is around 45 mm×37 mm, which is much smaller than that of the traditional printed monopole antenna. By utilizing electromagnetic simulation software CST, the antenna is simulated and optimized. A sample antenna is manufactured and measured to verify the predictive performance of the proposed antennas. The measured results are in agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Low-Profile LTE / WWAN / GPS Antenna System Placed on the Bezel of the Laptop
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a low profile LTE / WWAN/ GPS antenna system placed on the bezel of the laptop. The size of the antenna is 70 × 12.5 × 3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, which is designed for LTE/ WWAN and GPS applications. The antenna system is composed of a monopole antenna group and a shorting loop antenna. The high frequency band (1710-2690 MHz) and the GPS frequency (1575 MHz) are excited by the feed monopole antenna group, and the low frequency band (698-960 MHz), It is excited by the loop antenna which is formed by the coupling of the monopole antenna group branch and the shorting circuit metal plane. Then add 70 × 3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> metal plane on the shorting-circuit metal plane to increase the radiation area so that the low frequency band has a better operation bandwidth covering the LTE / WWAN frequency band. Finally, the actual installation of the antenna system on the laptop's bezel also results in good antenna characteristics.

articleTitle: Highly-Integrated Millimeter-Wave Wideband Slot-Type Array Antenna for 5G Mobile Phones
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A highly-integrated wideband slot-type array antenna formed using parallel-connected dual open-slots as the array element for 5G mobile phones is presented. The proposed wideband millimeter-wave array antenna can achieve 5.6 GHz bandwidth (-10 dB S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> definition) from 23.9~29.5 GHz to cover the whole 26 GHz and 28 GHz bands (n258 and n257 bands) of 3GPP 5G NR specification. A 4-element linear array antenna prototype is implemented by using simple printed circuit board (PCB) process for experimental study. The 4-element linear array antenna occupies a small layout area of 21.3×1.64 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at the short side edge of a PCB. Results show that wide-coverage fan-shape beamforming patterns and wide beam scanning coverage about 120 degrees can be achieved.

articleTitle: A Frequency Reconfigurable Patch Antenna/Array for S-Band and Ku-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A frequency reconfigurable patch antenna/array for S-band and K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub>-band applications is presented. The proposed antenna/array can be operated as a patch antenna in the lower frequency band or as a 2×2 patch array in the higher frequency band by forward or backward biasing the PIN diodes loaded in the structure. Therefore the operating frequency of the antenna can be switched between 3.4 GHz and 12.1 GHz. The simulated directivities of antenna/array are 5.95dBi and 11.3dBi respectively under two biasing conditions. The overall size of this antenna simulation is 31.0 mm×35.0 mm.

articleTitle: Beam Scanning at Ka-Band by Using Reflective Programmable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A digital coding reflective programmable metasurface is presented to realize beam scanning at Ka-band. The metasurface is composed of 400 digital coding elements, and each element contains a Positive-Intrinsic-Negative diode. A horn antenna is used to illuminate the metasurface. By configuring the digital coding elements according to special coding schemes, the far fields scattered by the metasurface can be directed to different directions, hence realizing beam scanning. Simulations show that beam scanning scope covers 120 degrees, and the maximum value of realized gain is 22.6dBi. The capacity of beam scanning enables the presented programmable metasurface to be used in millimeter-wave wireless communications.

articleTitle: Decoupling technique based on frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Array antennas have always been a core component of wireless communication systems and have a key role in the development of wireless communication technologies. However, the coupling effect between array antennas has a bad influence on the whole antenna system. How to effectively suppress the mutual coupling between antennas is also the key technology of array antenna research. In this paper, an decoupling technique based on frequency selective surface is proposed. The technique is placed the designed frequency selective surface structure directly above the array antenna, so that the the generated diffraction wave created by electromagnetic wave which passing through the frequency selective surface structure can reduce the coupling wave between antenna elements .Through model simulation, the proposed array antenna with the frequency selective surface achieves a coupling suppression of -34 dB over its operating frequency.

articleTitle: Electrically Small, Planar Dual-band Quasi-Isotropic Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel, yet simple design of a quasi-isotropic antenna which can operate at dual-band frequencies. The proposed antenna is electrically small and planar. The basic design configuration is based on the combination of electrically small electric and magnetic dipoles and the dual band operation is achieved by the additional parallel magnetic and electric dipole pair to the design for the single frequency operating. The electrical size of the antenna ka is 0.48. The proposed antenna can resonate at the frequencies of 917 MHz and 1.71 GHz. The maximum gain deviation at each frequency is found to be 3.16 dB and 5.5 dB, respectively from the computed expectations. The fabrication of the prototype and the experimental validation is undergoing and will be updated at the conference.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-Circuital-Thermal Co-Simulation for Integrated Circuits and Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The electromagnetic-circuital-thermal co-simulation method is introduced for integrated circuits and microwave applications. The time domain numerical method is adopted for electromagnetic and thermal simulation. The equivalent circuit model, equivalent physical model and the behavior macromodel are utilized for circuit modeling. Coupling interfaces are constructed for electromagnetic-circuital-thermal co-simulation. Numerical examples are given to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Planar Filtenna Array Implemented by Embedding the Filtering Function into the SIW Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel filtenna (filtering antenna) array is proposed and implemented by embedding the passband filtering function into the power divider feeding network. The proposed array antenna combines filtering, power division and radiation functions according to the classical coupling matrix theory. Besides, the antenna is built in one-layer substrate to achieve low profile and high integration goals. A substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) fourth-order Chebyshev filter is co-designed and embedded into the power divider and the slot radiation elements. The measured impedance matching, gain, and radiation patterns closely agree with simulation results. The center frequency and fractional bandwidth are 24.55GHz and 4.48%, respectively. The measured gain at the center frequency is 7.7dB, and the radiation gain performs a significant filtering characteristic.

articleTitle: An Equivalent Magnetic Current Array Model for Analysis of UWB Omnidirectional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a basic dipole antenna unit is designed to achieve stable UWB omnidirectional radiation through CST simulation.Antennas with different structures are obtained based on changing the number N of the antenna unit. The impedance bandwidth of several antennas presented in this paper all reach 70:1. Meantime, an equivalent magnetic current array theory model is also proposed to analyze the radiation mechanism of designed antennas. The proposed theory model is useful to study the condition when the out-of-roundness in H-plane pattern of the designed antenna is less than 3 dB. Calculation results of the presented magnetic current theory model are in good agreement with the simulation results, which show great value in guiding design of similar combined UWB omnidirectional antennas.

articleTitle: Abnormal Refraction THz Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Metasurface is an artificial layered material with a thickness less than the wavelength. It can flexibly and effectively manipulate electromagnetic wave, such as polarization, amplitude, phase, and propagation mode. In this paper, we proposed an abnormal refraction THz metasurface consisting of the silicon cubic resonator. By adjusting the geometry of cubic silicon resonator, the transmission phase coverage rang from -3π/4 to π is obtained. It is shown that the proposed metasurface can achieve the anomalous refraction at the THz band.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Frequency Selective Rasorber with an Absorptive Band between Two Transmission Bands
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel dual-polarized frequency selective rasorber. Based on an equivalent circuit model, the operation principle and design method are studied and analyzed. The rasorber exhibits an absorption band between two transmission bands. The lossy layer is achieved by introducing four resistors into a square loop slot, which contributes to the absorption band from 4.08GHz to 9.84GHz. The bottom layer is configured with a square loop slot with parasitic U-slots. Simulations are carried out and show that. From outside to inside, under the normal incidence, the insertion loss of the rasorber is about -1.23dB at 3.68GHz and -1.65dB at 9.22 GHz. In the meantime, the reflection is less than -10dB from 4.08GHz to 9.84GHz, a relative bandwidth of 83%. From inside to outside, the structure behaves as a dual-band pass filter. The insertion loss of the rasorber performance is about -1.25dB at 3.66GHz and the other one is about -1.47dB at 9.28GHz. For the two cases of oblique incidence of 30°, the rasorber can still maintain a good performance. Therefore, the proposed rasorber has a good application prospect in broadband stealth equipment with duplex communication.

articleTitle: A Deployable Metamaterial Reflectarray Antenna for Microsatellite Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a deployable high gain reflectarray antenna for microsatellite application is proposed. The reflectarray antenna is designed by using metamaterial graded quasi parabolic deployable reflector and radiator operating at 35.75 GHz. A highly reflecting metasurface with 3 dB stop band of more than 10 GHz bandwidth with maximum reflection at 35.75 GHz is designed. The phase graded modified circular ring resonator unit cells are used to design quasi parabolic phase distribution reflector. A gain of more than 12 dBi by small reflector antenna and more than 45 dBi by larger deployable reflector antenna is observed. The designed deployable reflector antenna is found to be suitable for microsatellite applications due to small volume, small weight and low cost.

articleTitle: Wideband Millimeter-wave Array Antenna Using Highly Conductive Graphene Film
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a wideband and high gain millimeter wave array antenna based on highly conductive graphene film is designed, fabricated and tested. The proposed antenna consists of 4×4 radiation patches and a Chebyshev feed network, which are made of highly conductive multilayer graphene film with light weight and low cost. The simulated and measured results show that the highly conductive graphene printed antenna array can achieve a high gain of 17.5-18.7dBi and wide bandwidth from 22.7GHz to 25.2GHz. The comparison between the proposed antenna and the traditional metal antenna implies that the highly conductive graphene film has great potential in array antenna design and millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Hybrid Method of MLFMA-HOMoM for Solving Radiation Problems of Radome System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Solving the radiation characteristics of radome system is always an important topic in the field of computational electromagnetics. However, for the target with complex antenna and a high number of unknowns, it is a challenging work to get accurate solution. A method based on the multilevel fast multipole algorithm hybridized with the higher order method of moments is proposed. Based on the idea of divide and conquer, the MLFMA handles with the radome region while the HOMoM deals with the antenna region, making it possible to handle with big radome system with millions of unknowns.

articleTitle: Broadband Center-fed Waveguide Linear Array Composed of Double-Slotted Cavity Sub-arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A center-fed narrow wall slotted waveguide linear array antenna composed of double slotted cavity sub-arrays was designed. There is a need for a simple antenna of a one-dimensional traveling-wave array. Narrow wall slotted waveguide arrays can be assembled at the center of the broad wall of the waveguide, where the high-frequency current is not cut. However, slot spacing of longitudinal slots is one guided wavelength, which generates grating lobes. We propose a linear array antenna composed of sub-arrays with cavity backed slots to arrange two slots excited in-phase with a half guided wavelength spacing. Consequently, no grating lobe appears in the radiation pattern. The simulated bandwidth of reflection lower than -10dB was 16.8GHz. The gain was 18.6dBi at 79GHz.

articleTitle: A Wide-Beam Quadrifilar Helical Antenna with High Gain at Low Elevation Angle for BDS Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wide-beam quadrifilar helical antenna (QHA) loaded with a parasitic cross dipole is presented in this paper. This antenna is designed especially for BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS), which requires broad beamwidth and high gain at low elevation angle. Additionally, an optimized structure of the antenna is proposed. In this way, the size of antenna won't increase. The final results demonstrate that the proposed antenna behaves a hemispherical radiation pattern with high gain (over 0.4 dB) at the elevation angle of 0°, broad 3-dB beamwidth (over 190 degree) and wide axial ratio bandwidth. This antenna can work normally at any elevation angle, which is feasible for application when the carrier of antenna is unstable and slant.

articleTitle: Online Diagnostic High Voltage Polymeric Outdoor Insulation Using Patch Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To realize an online diagnosis system for accurate detection of internal defects in high voltage polymeric outdoor insulations, a novel patch antennas system which would detect the transmission signal level difference caused by internal defects of insulations is proposed. In this work, investigation by simulation is performed with regard to the conventional interfacial mm-ordered cracks in both transverse and longitudinal orientations in one kind of insulation, namely insulator. Receiving signal differences of 30-50 dB and 30-60 dB between insulators with and without defects have been observed over 1-10 GHz, respectively to transverse and longitudinal defects. The proposed method by patch antennas system is promising to realize online diagnostic high voltage polymeric outdoor insulations with defects.

articleTitle: Study on Scattering Calculation of Typical Surface by AIEM Method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the use of advanced integral equation models (AIEM). Then we will use this method to study the backscattering coefficients of bare soil, cement and sand in different frequency bands, and compare the measured data to verify the applicability of the AIEM model in the scattering calculation of typical surface.

articleTitle: Equivalently Folded Lens-based Beamforming Networks for Antenna Size Reduction and Efficiency Enhancement in Multi-Beam Radiation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the size reduction of two-dimensional (2-D) lens based beamforming network (BFN) by equivalently folding the lens structure on the same substrate which is sandwiched by a pair of parallel plates. This in-same-substrate folding is realized by building a conducting wall at the middle of lens to apply the image theory and conceptually resemble the configuration of the original BFN lens. This technique is examined by applying it to design single beam and multi-beam BFN for planar array excitation. Various configurations are examined to illustrate this folding technique with numerical results shown to validate the design. Its examples in the phased array antenna radiation are also shown.

articleTitle: A Study of Grating Lobe Suppression in Linear Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A simple structure of the slot with baffle is introduced for suppressing the grating lobe of the linear array. The element space can be larger than one wavelength while the grating lobes of the array can be suppressed entirely. The proposed structure has achieved to suppress the grating lobes and to enhance the gain.

articleTitle: Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna Using Fractals and DGS for Wi-Fi Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Polarization reconfigurable antenna has been an interesting solution in increasing transmission efficiency. However, existing implementations tend to have low gain and limited bandwidth. In this work, design improvements for both gain and bandwidth was applied to a single-layered microstrip patch antenna with parasitic patches. Fractal implementation on the parasitic patches and main patch were used for both gain and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> improvement respectively. Circular Defected Ground Structures (DGS) with a 45 tilt was used to increase the ̊ bandwidth of the design. Simulation results showed the design having a center frequency of 2.4 GHz, a gain of 7.55 dBi, and bandwidth of 144 MHz.

articleTitle: A High Gain Broadband Vertically Polarized Omnidirectional Printed Antenna for Aircraft Surface Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a high gain broadband vertically polarized omnidirectional printed antenna for aircraft surface application. In order to achieve gain improvement, a printed choke sleeve, which can eliminate the influence of the radiation from the feeding coaxial line and the ground plane on the proposed antenna, is introduced between the feeding coaxial line and the antenna radiator. The omnidirectional gains range from 3.90 dBi to 5.64 dBi in the operating band of 4.40-5.50 GHz, which is 2.9 dB better than that of the conventional omnidirectional antenna without the choke sleeve. The proposed antenna possesses the characteristics of omnidirectional, broadband and high gains. It can be used on aircraft application.

articleTitle: Conformal Transmitarray and Its Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A mechanically beam-scanning conformal transmitarray is developed in this paper. Firstly, a transmitarray element with three layers of identical square ring slots is proposed and its performance for different element thickness is studied. A transmission phase range of 330° with a maximum 3.6 dB loss can be achieved when the thickness is 0.508mm (only 0.04 wavelength at 25GHz). Secondly, a cylindrically conformal transmitarray is designed using the above antenna elements, realizing a 45.3% simulated antenna efficiency. Finally, the above fixed-beam conformal transmitarray is expanded to a beam scanning one. By rotating the feed horn to different positions, the main beam of the array can be switched to ±15°, ±10°, ±5° and 0°, while the whole size of this array is only 2.5 times larger than the fixed beam one. A prototype is fabricated and measured with a stable gain of about 18.7 dBi at all beam angles.

articleTitle: Antenna Measurement System using Low Power Consumption Optical Fiber Link up to 40 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have already proposed a simple optical fiber link antenna measurement system using 850 nm multi-mode VCSEL and PD-TIA based antenna measurement system up to 17 GHz. However, 5th generation mobile network will use 3.7 GHz band, 4.5 GHz band, 28 GHz band and 38 GHz band.In this paper, we have newly developed low power consumption type low cost antenna measurement system using 850 nm multi-mode VCSEL and PD-TIA. Our proposed system can be measured the microwave signal up to 40 GHz that can measure -50 dBm input signal with 0.4 dB deviation.

articleTitle: Design of Metallic PhC Band-Pass Filter in Quasi-Millimeter-Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A metallic photonic crystal (M-PhC) structure, consisting of a periodic alignment of via holes in a low-loss printed circuit board, has characteristics such as small-size, lightweight, high-Q and planar-circuit integration and has great potential as a platform for various electromagnetic wave circuits. In this paper, a 5-pole inline-type bandpass filer is designed and realized in terms of coupling matrix synthesis technique in quasi-millimeter-wave regime. The measured characteristics of the filter compare well with the theoretical and simulated ones, which validates the proposed structure and the corresponding design method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Coupling Slots with a Reflection-canceling Wall for Parallel Plate Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A center-feed parallel plate slot array antenna with hard walls which supports a TEM wave is proposed for millimeter wave application. Coupling slots of the feeder network are analyzed and designed by method of moment (MoM). It is shown that computation time by using MoM is drastically reduced compared to HFSS. The design parameter relationship between HFSS and MoM models is found for compensating the inaccuracy caused by simplified assumption in the MoM model.

articleTitle: Scattering Center Models for Dielectric Plates Based on PO+PTD
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Scattering center models specific for dielectric plates are proposed based on physical optics (PO) and physical optics of diffraction theory (PTD). Based on the proposed models, the scattering components under different polarizations are analyzed. The models are validated by comparing the numerical results computed by the models and by a full-wave numerical method. The radar cross-section (RCS) and the time-frequency representation (TFR) results demonstrate that the scattering center models proposed in this paper for the dielectric plates are of high precision.

articleTitle: Metasurface lens for generating independent tri-foci with different polarizations
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a novel reflective metasurface lens (or meta-lens) combining geometric phase and propagation phase to realize a multifunctional electromagnetic (EM) device. The proposed meta-lens can generate distinct focal spots of different polarizations under the linear polarized incidence. In order to verily the concept, we have integrated three foci of different polarizations with distinct focal positions into a single meta-lens. We have fabricated the meta-lens and good agreements are observed between the measurement and simulation, and they are both consistent with theoretical prediction. This method could pave a new way to design multi-functional devices for generating diverse wavefronts with different polarizations.

articleTitle: Investigation of plasmon hybridization between slot-ring resonator absorber and lattice pattern substrate
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the mechanism of SRR absorber permittivity control by plasmon hybridization at 120 GHz band. We have already shown that the permittivity of SRR absorber increases by 33 dB by opposing the lattice pattern substrate close to SRR absorber via 50-μm-thick spacer. We have found that the 3-dB passband bandwidth of SRR substrate increased to 113-126 GHz when the distance between two substrates was reduced by using 20-μm-thick spacer, which improves the broadband data transmission characteristics. We have simulated the electric field vector between SRR absorber and lattice pattern substrate in order to clarify the mechanism of plasmon hybridization between the SRR absorber and the lattice pattern substrate, and found that modes of plasmon hybridization between SRR absorber and lattice pattern substrate are different from that between SRR absorbers.

articleTitle: On-Body Channel Characteristics Based on Variation of Human Tissue Properties
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Effects of tissue property in the on-body communications were investigated in this paper. First, to simplify the human body modeling, homogeneous human models were constructed for different frequencies and their accuracies were discussed. It turned out that from the path loss point of view, muscle equivalent model provides a good approximation for low frequency propagation while skin equivalent model is more accurate at high frequency. Then, the variabilities of path loss for the belt-to-chest link as the result of tissue property changes were examined. The mean and standard deviation of path loss exponent were presented from which the limits of path loss can be determined. Results showed that tissue property has larger impact at low frequency.

articleTitle: A Uniplanar Multi-Band Antenna for The Metal Back Cover Tablet Computer Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research proposes a multi-band antenna which is composed of an inverted-F antenna and a parasitic short-circuit monopole. The size of this antenna is 60 mm × 10 mm × 0.8 mm and this antenna is fabricated on a FR4 glass epoxy substrate. This uniplanar antenna is compact and simple structure, and designs on the metal back cover tablet computer. The operating frequency bands of this antenna includes the LTE 700/900/1800 and WLAN 2.4/5 GHz bands. The efficiency and peak gain are 35%-77% and -0.82 dBi-5 dBi respectively.

articleTitle: Simple Evaluation Method of Residual Aberration Using Radius of Curvature in Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a simple evaluation method for the residual aberration of a reflectarray antenna using aberration theory is proposed. It is shown that the aberration is a part of the ellipsoid, and the residual aberration can be evaluated simply by approximating the radius of curvature to a spherical wave. The validity of the method by analysis and theoretical formula is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design of a Pin-loaded Wideband Implantable Antenna with Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a pin-loaded circularly polarized antenna that operating at the 2.45-GHz industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) band is designed for biomedical applications. Its circularly polarized wave is generated by the loading of vias and two arc-shaped open slots, where the two slots have different lengths to achieve better axial-ratio (AR) performance. Besides, the antenna size is miniaturized by loading two pairs of patches at the inner edge of annular ring. In addition, we loaded a notch on the ring near the feed point to improve the matching performance and achieve a wide impedance bandwidth. This proposed structure shows a simulated impedance bandwidth of 9.7% and a wide AR bandwidth of 15.9%. Finally, the radiation patterns and specific absorption rate performance of the antenna are characterized, showing it a satisfying candidate for implantable applications.

articleTitle: Reduction of Correlation Coefficient in Wideband MIMO Antennas using Partially Reflective Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents a technique to reduce the Correlation Coefficient (CC) of a wideband Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna using wideband partially reflective surfaces (PRS). The proposed design of the PRS acts as a superstrate over the MIMO antenna forming a wideband Fabry-Perot Cavity (FPC). The introduction of the cavity reduces the beamwidth of antenna elements, which in turn reduces the overlap between the beams and reduces the CC of the MIMO antenna system. A wideband parasitic patch antenna operating from 9 GHz to 10.4 GHz is used to validate the effectiveness of proposed design. Simulated far-field results have been used to calculate the CC for which a 35-63% reduction is achieved with a bandwidth of 12.5%.

articleTitle: E.M. Characterization of Common Construction Materials Using the Fabry-Pérot resonance method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Several frequency bands above 6 GHz are being proposed for next generation wireless systems, and the electromagnetic characteristics of many common construction materials at these frequencies still need to be determined. The knowledge of such characteristics is particularly relevant, especially in relation to the increasing use of deterministic propagation models for radio-channel characterization in 5G and beyond systems. In this study, an assessment of the method based on Fabry-Pérot resonance for the evaluation of the complex permittivity of construction materials is presented. The method is shown to be effective in several cases using a relatively simple VNA-based measurement setup and procedure. We also present a comparison between VNA results and measurements performed with a spectrum compact analyzer. The aim is to show that it is possible to perform evaluation of electromagnetic characteristics of materials with a portable, handy and easy-to-use kit, leading to carry out on-site evaluation, without the necessity to acquire a sample of the material and to perform ad-hoc measurements in anechoic room.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Sparse Planar Arrays Using Off-grid CS
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel method for the synthesis of sparse planar arrays with prescribed pattern features is presented. Unlike conventional compressed sensing (CS) approach, the active elements are not assumed to lie on the pre-specified grids, but can be randomly distributed in the given array aperture. Towards this end, the synthesis problem is formulated as a ridge regression model with the element excitations and locations all unknows. The alternative optimization strategy can be adopted herein to solve the synthesis model by estimating the layout and the excitation of the sparse planar array, simultaneously. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed method in the reduction of the number of elements as well as reconstructing the desired focused pattern and flat-top pattern accurately.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction of Closely E/H-coupled MIMO Antennas through Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposed a simple metasurface for mutual coupling reduction of E/H-coupled MIMO antennas. The proposed metasurface is consisted of periodic "H" shaped slots arranged on one side of the substrate. The metasurface can improve the isolation of both E/H-coupled antennas by neutralizing the near-field coupling. The experimental results show that the achieved isolation is better than 20 dB and the maximum isolation enhancement is 30 dB, with an edge-to-edge separation of just 0.023°0. The prototypes of E/H-coupled antennas with metasurfaces are fabricated, and the experimental measurements and the simulation results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Design a Ku Dual-band Hat-Fed Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A ku dual-band hat-fed reflector antenna is presented in this paper. Firstly, a new phase efficiency calculation model is employed for calculating phase efficiency of hat-fed accurately. By that method, accurate results can be obtained compared with former works. Secondly, the model of the hat feed is established by ANSOFT HFSS. Based on GA algorithms, a satisfying efficiency of the hat feed for reflector is obtained. Then, the OMT is designed. Finally, a ku dual-band hat-fed reflector antenna is proposed. The simulated results show that the proposed hat fed reflector antenna has a VSWR of less than 1.23 and an aperture efficiency of higher than 70% in the lower band (12.25-12.75GHz) and a VSWR of less than 1.16 and an aperture efficiency of higher than 71.2% in the higher band(14-14.5GHz).

articleTitle: The Design of Dual-Sense Circularly Polarized Series-Fed Microstrip Patch Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual circularly polarized traveling wave series-fed microstrip patch array working at 24 GHz is proposed. The antenna array consists of eight slotted patches each of which can produce circularly polarized waves. With two ports at both ends of the series-fed array, a dual-sense circularly polarized narrow-beam high-gain antenna is obtained when the dual ports are excited respectively. The simulated results show that the array achieves a good overlap bandwidth of impedance bandwidth (IBW) and axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) from 23.63 GHz to 25.25 GHz (6.63%). Excellent radiation patterns with low back lobes and cross polarization are obtained over the entire band of operation.

articleTitle: Measurement of Reflection and Transmission Characteristics of Glasses at 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We evaluated the reflection and transmission characteristics of 7 types of glasses used as building materials at a frequency of 220-320 GHz. In case the incident angle is 0 degree, reflection characteristics is almost the same regardless of the types of the glasses. Transmission characteristics depends only on the thickness of glasses except for heat absorbing plate glass. We measured the dependence of reflection characteristics on the incident angle, and used it as a parameter of materials in the propagation simulation. The indoor propagation simulation results using the measured reflection characteristics of glasses indicates that the reflection at high incident angle in our model is larger than that of ITU-R model.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Circularly Polarized Crossed-Dipole Antenna with Band-Notch Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized antenna operating over frequency range of 1.61-6.18GHz with band-notch performance for 3.58-3.75GHz is presented. The antenna is composed of two orthogonally placed elliptical dipoles printed on both sides of a substrate above a square cavity, which is fed by a coaxial cable and two ring-shaped phase delay lines that introduce a 90°phase difference between the adjacent elliptical arms on the same side. For achieving a band-notch characteristic, four slot-type spilt ring resonators (SRR) have been etched on each of the arms. The bandwidth and central frequency of the notched band can be adjusted by modifying the size of SRRs. Characteristics of the presented antenna have been investigated in terms of the impedance bandwith, AR bandwith, realized gain and radiation pattern. The simulated results confirm that the proposed antenna has good performance for Ultra-Wideband applications.

articleTitle: A Wideband Microstrip Patch Antenna with Dual Square Open-loop Resonators
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband microstrip patch antenna (MPA) with a pair of square open-loop resonators is proposed. Initial, a low-profile U-slot MPA with the conventional aperture-coupled feeding is designed. The second resonant mode is excited around the fundamental mode of the MPA due to the introduced U-slot on the radiating patch. Then, by employing a square open-loop resonator on the feeding line, the antenna achieves an addition resonant mode around its original modes. After that, an identical square open-loop resonator is further added for the bandwidth enhancement. In final, the proposed MPA is simulated and studied. The results illustrate that the impedance bandwidth of the antenna with two square open-loop resonators is successfully extended to about 10.72%, while keeping a low profile of about 0.04 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength). Meanwhile, a stable gain varied from 4.63 to 7.88 dBi is acquired within the whole operating band.

articleTitle: A Microfluidically Frequency-Reconfigurable Quasi-Yagi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A frequency reconfigurable Quasi-Yagi Antenna using liquid metal alloy is presented. The length of the driven elements can be tuned with pressure-driven liquid metal, resulting in tunable frequency of the proposed antenna. At different operating frequencies, the length of the director is changed with the same method to maximize the end-fire gain of the antenna. The measured operating frequency is from 1.79GHz to 4.8GHz, and the gain range is 3.06~4.95dBi.

articleTitle: Metasurface-based Polarization Insensitive Absorber for C, X, Ku and K bands Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a metasurface-based multiband absorber in microwave frequency regime. The proposed metasurface absorbs electromagnetic (EM) waves in four different frequency bands: C-Band (7.75 - 7.88 GHz), X-band (11.084 - 11.183 GHz), Ku Band (13.99 - 14.22 GHz) and Ka Band (18.185 - 18.993 GHz). The unit cell of the periodic metasurface consists of a metallic star-shaped structure printed on 2.4mm thick FR4 substrate backed by a metallic ground plane. The full-wave numerical results show that absorption efficiencies are above 90% in all frequency bands. The C4-symmetry of the unit cell makes the response of metasurface exactly same for both x- and y-polarized incident waves.

articleTitle: A Study of Multiple Image Acquisition on Stripmap SAR for Wide Beam Antenna and High Squint Case
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces the theoretical explanation of verifying the multiple image acquisition method on Stripmap SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar). This technique is needed for generating video images when wide beam antenna and high squint conditions are satisfied. It also explains why wide beam antenna and high squint case conditions are required. Furthermore, we show the simulation results using the hypothetical static point target to prove the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Block Maximum SNR Algorithm for MU-MIMO System under Rice Fading Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: MU-MIMO has been considered as a fundamental technology for simultaneous communications between a base station and multiple users. This paper compares the performances of MMSE-CI, BD and BMSN algorithms under the Rice fading environment.

articleTitle: Low Profile Broadband Cavity-Backed Patch Phased Array Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a low profile broadband phased array antenna based multilayer low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology for system-in-package (SIP) applications operating at millimeter-wave band. The radiating element is fed by a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) aperture, and U-shaped patch is used to broaden antenna bandwidth, in addition that a SIW cavity is introduced to decrease mutual coupling between adjacent antennas. The total antenna thickness including feeding SIW is 0.9 mm (about 0.1 λ at 35 GHz). Simulated results show that the active VSWR below 2.5 ranges from 32 to 37.6 GHz (16.1%) while scanning up to 60° in E-plane and 45° in H-Plane. Then a 7 × 7 phased array is simulated, the results show that when scanning angle is 60° in E-plane and 45° in H-plane at 35 GHz, peak gain decreases about 3 dB and 1.8 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: On Near-Field 2-D target imaging by Using Khatri-Rao Product Extended Array Processing
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The main objective in this study is to realize imaging radar of human-body check for security with small number of observation point or array elements. In this paper, we study the application of Khatri-Rao product virtual array processing to relative near-field SAR data for 2-D imaging. Computer simulation was performed using Beamformer as the imaging method. Simulation results with the mode vector under the far-field approximation and the near-field were compared. The results show that the imaging results can be improved by using the near-field mode vector.

articleTitle: An Omnidirectional Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an omnidirectional circularly polarized antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide. The proposed CP antenna has a simple structure with a single feed. The antenna can be considered as a superimposition of two circular cavities. Two orthogonal TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> modes are then generated to achieve an omnidirectional CP radiation pattern. Parasitical strips are used for impedance matching. The antenna has a 10-dB impedance fractional bandwidth range from 4.29 GHz to 4.38 GHz. The axial ratio (AR) of the proposed antenna is 0.6 dB at 4.31 GHz.

articleTitle: Compact UWB Microstrip Antenna with 3.5/5.5-GHz Dual Band-Notched Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed compact ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna with dual band-notched characteristics is presented in this paper. The antenna consists of a trophy-shaped monopole radiator and a slotted ground plane extended toward two sides of the monopole radiator. By adding a pair of quarter-wavelength parasite branches at the top part of the ground, and etching a screw-shaped meandering slot into the junction of the feed line and the radiating patch, the dual band-notched characteristics centered at 3.5 GHz and 5.5 GHz are achieved, respectively. The proposed antenna has a compact size of 25 × 28 mm with stable omnidirectional radiation patterns in the working bands, and operates in 2.63-11.3 GHz, which is a promising candidate for UWB applications.

articleTitle: Automobile Anti-Collision Warning Radar Antennas with Tapered Excitations at Millimeter Wave Frequencies and their Design Consideration
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a set of phased arrays of antennas are developed for automobile anti-collision warning applications at 76GHz of millimeter wave (mmW) frequencies. This antenna set consists of two 16×8 and one 16×1 series-fed tapered antenna arrays for both long- and short-distance target detections. This antenna set has a radiation gain up to 24dBi and relative sidelobe level of smaller than -20dB in both E- and H planes by implementing a Dolph-Chebyshev distribution of excitation weightings. The return loss of power divider is lower than 25dB. The design consideration incorporating the PCB board effects is also studied to examine the radiation distortion in practical applications. Numerical simulation results are shown to validate the radiation phenomenon while measured data will be shown in the conference presentation.

articleTitle: Reference Signal Reconstruction Method Considering Delayed Wave for TDL Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In multipath environment, a desired directional pattern cannot be formed by array antennas due to delayed signals such as reflected waves. As the results, communication quality may be degraded. This paper proposes a new reference signal reconstruction method using a delay profile and original reference signal. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Low Profile VHF Airborne Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel low profile antenna working at VHF band (96.8MHz-100.5MHz) with vertical polarization has been designed for airborne application. Except for the traditional Yagi structure, top-hat loaded elements and a transmission element was designed to reduce the profile height and achieve a good impedance match. Compared to conventional vertical polarization antenna, this antenna has an extremely low profile of 0.07λ at its lowest operating frequency. The presented array antenna with 2×3 elements would realize ±30° beam scanning capability in the horizontal plane and generate a peak gain of 8.5dBi in whole band.

articleTitle: Wide-band Wide-beam Circular Polarization Cone-plane Composite Helical Millimeter-wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In millimeter wave band, the width of the antenna arm of the planar helical antenna is difficult to be sufficiently small because of the processing accuracy. It results in a decrease in the circular polarization performance of the antenna at high frequencies. In this paper, the 3D structure of a conical and planar composite spiral is used. This configuration does not require changing the width of the antenna arm. At the same time, the spiral density of the antenna arm is increased. This makes the Axial Ratio of circular polarization better at high-frequency. Also it can reduce the difficulty in processing the antenna arm.

articleTitle: Experimental wireless channel analysis between 1 and 40 GHz in an indoor NLoS corridor environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents an analysis of the wireless channel based on a measurement campaign performed from 1 GHz to 40 GHz in an Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) indoor corridor environment. The delay characteristics and path loss parameters are estimated for different sub-bands. The NLoS values are compared with Line-of-Sight (LoS) results extracted from the same measurement campaign. The channel sounder is based on a Vector Network Analyzer, one linear positioning system and Optical-Radio transceivers. The positioning system allows the measurement of MIMO channel transfer functions. These functions are measured without distance limitation thanks to the fiber-optic system.

articleTitle: Enhance the Optical Intensity of a Photomixer Based THz Antenna Using a Two Dimentional Photonic Crystal
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A photomixer with plasmonic electrodes has been considered on a low temperature grown Gallium Arsenide, LT-GaAs. A two dimensional photonic crystal, 2D-PhC, has been incorporated to act as a reflector that conserves more optical power in the LT-GaAs. As a result, the photomixer generated terahertz power has been enhanced. Simulated results demonstrate that enhancement of 62% has been achieved in the optical E field amplitude. Therefore, the generated THz power can be improved by a factor of 6.9 for the same incident optical source.

articleTitle: Wideband Design of a 350GHz-band Corporate-feed Waveguide Slot Array Antenna using Gold-coating Silicon Wafers with Different Thickness
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the radiating element of 2×2 slots is designed for a 350 GHz-band corporate-feed waveguide slot array antenna using gold-coating silicon wafers with different thickness (30 μm, 180 μm, and 275 μm) to improve the bandwidth. A 20.0% bandwidth for the reflection less than -15 dB is achieved. The bandwidth for VSWR less than 1.5 in a 16×16-slot array with a feeding circuit is 18.7% by simulation. The aperture efficiency and the antenna efficiency at the center frequency of 362.5 GHz are 94.3% and 85.4%, respectively.

articleTitle: 2D-DOA Estimation by Compressed Sensing Using Sub-Arrays in an Actual Urban Street Cell Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a compressed sensing is applied to actual measurement data acquired in an actual urban street cell environment by a 20GHz band channel sounder. Then, accuracy of vertical and horizontal 2D-DOA estimation is evaluated. It is shown that the estimation accuracy is improved by using sub-array process and eigenbeam.

articleTitle: Design of Two-dimensional Microstrip Planar Arrays for Arbitrary Linear Polarizations Using Rounded Radiating Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Two-dimensional microstrip array antenna for arbitrary linear polarizations were developed to achieve high-gain in this work. Microstrip antennas suffer from high feeding-loss in high frequency band. Therefore, a comb-line antenna with travelling-wave operation is applied. To reduce loss increasing due to manufacturing errors in millimeter-wave band and to realize an arbitrary linear polarization, we propose rounded radiating elements for comb-line antennas. The performance of the rounded radiating elements and its microstrip planar arrays with 30, 45, 60-degree linear polarization are evaluated in millimeter-wave band by simulations.

articleTitle: Design of Single Radiator Direction Finding Antenna Using SIW Feeders
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a multimode substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) feeding system with a single patch antenna for monopulse direction finding applications. The multimode feeding system allows to radiate the sum and difference patterns with a single radiator. The maximum gains of each sum and difference pattern are 2.1 dBi and -2.6 dBi, respectively. We then obtain a calibration factor that minimizes the RMSE of the angle of arrivals to 2.1°.

articleTitle: Triple-band EBG Reflector Using CPW Structure with Interdigital Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The electromagnetic band gap (EBG) unit cell was designed from mushroom-like EBG structure by adapting a coplanar waveguide (CPW) feed structure and interdigital technique on mushroom-like EBG. This new designed EBG is defined as interdigital coplanar waveguide (ICPW) structure. The proposed EBG can reduce the original mushroom-like EBG dimension from λ/2 to λ/4, which the ICPW-EBG unit cell dimension is 14.6x14.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The ICPW-EBG unit cell was designed to response three frequency bands at 1.8 GHz, 2.45 GHz and 3.7 GHz. The array of 10×10 ICPW-EBG unit cells was then formed with the dimension of 147.3x147.3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. When installing a dipole antenna above the ICPW-EBG array, the simulation results showed that the dipole antenna directivities at all frequency bands were improved from 2.15 dB to 9.12 dB at 1.8 GHZ, 9.05 dB at 2.45 GHz and 8.4 dB at 3.7 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-band Coupled-fed Dipole Antenna for PCL systems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article proposes the design of a dual-band coupled-fed dipole antenna element for PCL systems. The proposed coupled-fed antenna consists of an internal and an external dipoles which resonate in FM and DMB frequencies, respectively. To verify the suitability of the proposed coupled-fed antenna, antenna characteristics such as the bore-sight gain and reflection coefficient are compared with the conventional single dipole antenna. The results confirm that the proposed antenna structure can achieve the dual-band operation with broadband matching characteristic using the coupled-fed mechanism.

articleTitle: The application of Quasi-Conformal Transformation Optics to antenna array design
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Quasi-conformal transformation optics theory has been proven to be able to arbitrarily regulate electromagnetic waves. Especially in the case of two-dimensional TE polarization, the non-magnetic media can be used to construct the transformation space, which avoid narrowband and high loss properties of magnetic metamaterial. Based on the quasi-conformal transformation optics, the lens from transformations between virtual and physical arrays are designed in this paper. By loading the transformed lens on physical conformal and linear arrays respectively, the same radiation characteristics with the virtual arrays can be achieved in the corresponding physical spaces.

articleTitle: Amplitude- and phase-tailorable metasurface for circularly polarized low side-lobe antenna design
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) metasurfaces are capable of flexibly tailoring circularly polarized waves but still limited to the phase-only control. Here, we present a new strategy for realizing simultaneous amplitude and phase control of circularly polarized waves by combining propagation phase and the PB counterpart. As a proof of concept, a well-engineered spatial phase and amplitude distribution, which obeys the Tailor distribution, is employed to actualize a circularly polarized low side lobe antenna around 14 GHz. The finally assembled antenna well validates our strategy of simultaneous amplitude and phase control, achieving a directive beam of 20 dB with side lobe levels uniformly below -22.5 dB at 14 GHz. The proposed novel strategy for simultaneous amplitude and phase control of circularly polarized waves may pave the way for many fascinating meta-devices.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna for Wireless Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A polarization-reconfigurable (PR) antenna for wireless communication applications is proposed. The PR antenna consists of two PIN-diodes that work as a switch to generate the linear and circular polarization capabilities. This work presents the enhancement on gain and bandwidth of the PR antenna. The designs were simulated using CST Microwave Studio on FR4 board with dielectric constant of 4.7, loss tangent of 0.019 and thickness of 1.6mm. In order to improve the gain, directivity and bandwidth of the antenna, a simple superstrate is used along with array of patches. The simulation result shows that at the operating frequency of 5.8 GHz, the PR can increase the gain from 0.91 to 3.17 dBi and the directivity from 5.96 to 8.47 dBi.

articleTitle: Magneto-Electric Dipole Antennas with Polarization Diversity and Wide Overlapped Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper summarizes some of our recent studies on polarization reconfigurable antennas based on magneto-electric dipole featuring a wide overlapped bandwidth, a high efficiency and multiple polarization states. With focus on extending the overlapped bandwidth, the motivation, operation principle as well as the simulated and measured results will all be presented.

articleTitle: Compact Wideband Multi-Section Quarter-Wave-Like Transformers with Unequal Electrical Lengths
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes quarter-wave-like transformers (QWLTs) with unequal electrical lengths to miniaturize multi-section quarter wave transformers (QWTs) and to enhance the bandwidth. The proposed method extends a study of the approximate theory of small reflections (ATSR) for QWLTs called the extended approximate theory of small reflections (EATSR). The total input reflection coefficient is observed in the frequency range of interest. Results of the EATSR for both two-and three-section unit cells with 25% physical size reduction prove that their impedance bandwidths are broader than those of the standard multi-section QWTs and the ATSR for QWLTs.

articleTitle: A current probe calibration method for the application of loop antenna calibration
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The current probe of the current probe method (CPM) in the loop antenna calibration does not have a recommended calibration method which takes into consideration the loop connected to it, a method for current probe calibration considering the transmitting loop effect is proposed, and the uncertainty is analyzed. The method considers the current probe along with the loop as a three-port network, and derives the full parameter formula and a sampled formula for the transfer impedance of the current probe by using the S-parameter signal flow chart. The experimental results show that the difference between the measured and the nominal value of the transfer impedance is within 0.017Ω over 9kHz to 30MHz.

articleTitle: A Phased Array Element Antenna for Ka-Band Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A phased array element antenna for Ka-band satellite communication is designed in this paper. The antenna is composed of eight layers, and the working frequency of the antenna is 19.6-22GHz. The microstrip line is split into two parts in order to provide power to the two radiation patches which result in the phase difference of electric field radiation of 90°. This is the reason that circularly polarized waves are generated. Within the operating frequency, the max gain of the S11 is 6.7491dB with an omnidirectional radiation pattern in E-plane. The axial ratios are all below 3.5dB. The comparison between measured results and simulated results is also discussed.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Smart Antenna Using Active Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Smart antenna is a key technology for advanced wireless systems and one of the most important features of smart antenna is electronically beam scanning or switching. It is highly desirable to reduce the mass, power consumption and cost of smart antennas, as the traditional phased array is always associated with high cost due to the use of many T/R modules and complicated beamforming network (BFN). This paper presents the University of Kent's recent research progress in the field of low-cost smart antenna design using active frequency selective surfaces (AFSS). Firstly, this paper presents a brief review of AFSS based beam-reconfigurable antenna including several recent designs reported by the authors' group. Then, a new high-gain AFSS antenna design with some preliminary results will be presented. This is design achieves higher gain than the reported AFSS antennas. A detailed list of references is given at the end of this paper.

articleTitle: Compact 900-MHz LoRa Band Antenna On a Low-Profile AMC Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a low-profile AMC surface is used to secure the performance reliability of a LoRa module that can be installed under various construction site environments. The proposed low-profile 2 × 2 AMC has the thickness of 0.02λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> on the FR-4 substrate. A compact, planar meander antenna covering the LoRa band is designed. It is found that the impedance and radiation properties of the antenna in free space are maintained when it is placed on a concrete medium after it is backed by the proposed surface.
