articleTitle: The Aspects of Radome Performance Measurement in the Compact Range
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper the aspects of radome performance measurement in the compact range are discussed. It is found that special aspects regarding accuracy of measurement of radome in compact range should be taken into account such as repeatability, stability, linearity, calibration and so on.

articleTitle: Position estimation of capsule endoscope using high-definition numerical human body model
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Capsule endoscope is an innovative imaging device which offers less invasive procedure than conventional wired endoscope for the monitoring internal digestive tract in medical diagnosis. In order to improve the power transmission efficiency of the moving capsule, analysis on position estimation was conducted using Received Signal Strength algorithm in high-definition numerical human body model. As a result, an estimation error within 40 mm was achieved at about 80% of all the examination points.

articleTitle: Research of Wide Beam Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The design of a wide beamwidth antenna is presented in this paper. According to the current distribution characteristics of microstrip patch antenna and the near-field radiation characteristics, metal columns are loaded on the outside of the two symmetrical edges of the rectangular patch to which current flows vertically to complete the beam broadening. And the 3dB beamwidth of this antenna's E-plane is broaded from original 84 degrees to 120 degrees.

articleTitle: Ray-Tracing Based Millimeter-Wave Large-Scale Channel Characteristics in Corridor Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications play a crucial role to meet the anticipated demands of mobile traffic in the fifth generation (5G) and beyond wireless communication systems. Getting full knowledge of the propagation characteristics across different mmWave bands and scenarios is the basis of system design and deployment. In this paper, we investigate the large-scale channel characterizations in a typical corridor environment at 25.5 GHz and 39.5 GHz based on 3D ray-tracing simulations. Simulation results show that mmWave channel characteristics are sensitive to transceiver siting in terms of path loss, delay spread, and angular spread. Moreover, waveguide-like effect is obvious in corridor environment which results in not dramatically worse coverage probability at the two mmWave bands.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Gain Planar Antenna for Millimeter-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel wideband high-gain planar antenna is presented in this paper. The antenna element is composed of a Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed patch and a stepped waveguide horn. Based on the proposed antenna element, a 2×2 subarray with element spacing larger than a wavelength is designed. A groove, which worked as secondary radiation source, is etched between the elements to improve the gain and suppress the high sidelobes of the 2×2 sub-array. By taking the advantage of the groove, the 2×2 subarray achieves a maximum boresight gain of 17 dBi and an -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 21.8% from 70-87 GHz. For further enhancing the gain, a prototype including 16×16 elements is manufactured and measured. Experimental results confirm that the proposed antenna achieves an -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 22.4% from 71 to 88.5 GHz as well as a peak gain of 28.8-30.9 dBi.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Wideband Skeletal Spherical Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A skeletal spherical dipole antenna with similar radiation characteristics to Hertzian dipole is proposed in this paper. The antenna consists of a skeletal conical feed structure, a skeletal spherical dome loaded, and four metal arms connecting the two sides of the antenna. Even though with the size comparable to the operating wavelength at 1GHz, the antenna has the similar current distribution and radiation pattern to those of the Hertzian dipole. Besides, by employing the conical feed structure, the impedance bandwidth can reach to 52.15%. This antenna can be used in the research of the interaction between plasma and electromagnetic field.

articleTitle: Design of Compact and Efficient Superdirective Array with Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a compact and efficient superdirective antenna with parasitic elements optimized with a network characteristic mode approach is presented. To achieve high efficiency and bandwidth, compact superdirective array is realized using a wideband unit element in stacked configuration.

articleTitle: Layout Effects of MIMO Antennas in Handsets
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Designers of handsets employing Multi Input Multi Output (MIMO) antenna systems try to judiciously select the layout for best performance. Typically, the performance criteria invoked for such a design decision are focused on tuning the Multi Element Antenna (MEA) system and locating so as to ensure adequate radiation efficiency, return loss, isolation, Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) and impedance bandwidth with or without active matching. In this work we study the effect of the antenna element layout as manifested by a higher and more appropriate system-level performance metric, namely that of the resultant capacity under certain assumptions on the characteristics of the propagation environment and the base station antennas.

articleTitle: Broadband Center-Fed SIW Slot Array Antenna with Multi-Layer Transition for 79 GHz Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based broadband millimeter-wave slot array antenna is proposed for 79 GHz automotive radar applications. To halve the long-line effect and increase the impedance bandwidth, the antenna is fed by center-fed structure located at the bottom of SIW. To transmit energy through the multi-layer board to the antenna, two different vertical transitions are designed. Using the surrogate-model-assisted differential evolution for antenna synthesis (SADEA), the size of the slots, the offset of the slots and the positions of metallic via holes are optimized, which results in a low sidelobe level in the E-plane. The simulated 10 dB impedance bandwidth of the designed antenna is from 75.6 to 81.4 GHz and the realized gain is 10.5-12 dB within 76-81 GHZ frequency band. The results show that the proposed antenna can be applied to radar applications in 79 GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: Wideband Tunable Bandpass Frequency Selective Surface with Compact Size
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband tunable bandpass frequency selective surface with compact size is proposed in this paper. The proposed tunable FSS is composed of three layers with an entire size of 3.6mm×3.6mm×1.02mm.The upper and the bottom layer are identical in construction and there are four varactors loaded on each layer. The metal via which connects the three layers and the rectangular rings on the top and bottom layer provide the bias for the varactors. By applying different voltages to the varactor diode from 0V to 16V, the capacitance of the varactor changes from 0.12pF to 1pF and the center frequency of the FSS varies from 6.1GHz to 16.4GHz. The angular stability of the proposed FSS is also studied. As shown from the simulation results, when the angle of the incident wave changes from 0° to 60°, the presented FSS exhibits a good working performance under different bias voltages.

articleTitle: Design of a twelve-port MIMO Antenna for 5G/4G Smartphone Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact printed twelve-port MIMO antenna system for future multi-mode 5G/4G smartphone applications is presented. The proposed MIMO antenna system consists of 4G antenna module and 5G antenna module. The 4G antenna module is a 2×2 MIMO antenna array capable of covering the bands of 691-970, 1430-2740, and 3360-3960MHz. The operating bands of the 5G antenna module with S11 lower than -6dB ranges over 3.31~3.70GHz and 4.46~5.40GHz, covering the 3.5-GHz band (3.4~3.6GHz) and 4.9-GHz band (4.8~5.0GHz) for future 5G applications.

articleTitle: An Accurate Algorithm for Phase Center Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: the determination of the phase center with high accuracy is critical in many applications, especially in antenna far field phase pattern measurements. The particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO) and genetic algorithm (GA) is adopted to obtain the phase center of the antenna. Then, a comparison is done to show the difference between these two algorithms in finding of the phase center. Result gives that the PSO has a better performance in calculations speed than GA under the same calculation accuracy. At last. Some simulations are performed to ensure our conclusions.

articleTitle: A 1-bit Reflective Metasurface for Generating OAM Waves Based on Linear Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel 1-bit reflective metasurface to generate orbital angular momentum (OAM) waves in radio frequency domain. The metasurface unit cell is based on a wideband linear polarizer, which consists of a single-layer substrate with top polarization rotating patch (PRP) and bottom metallic ground. The proposed unit cell and its mirror image can maintain a stable 180° phase difference over a wide bandwidth of 18-36 GHz. Thus, 1-bit phase quantization is obtained by using this property. Based on the linear polarizer, a 1-bit reflectarray for generating +1 mode OAM waves is designed and simulated. The simulated results show that +1 mode OAM vortex electromagnetic waves are successfully generated and a small divergence angle of +/- 4° is obtained, with a high gain of 19.2 dBi at 27 GHz.

articleTitle: Integrated Design of Helix and Diplexer for S Band Mobile Communication Satellite Payload
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Integrated design approach of helix and diplexer is proposed which can be used in S band mobile communication satellite. The PIM test results of the prototype feed chain show that the specification has met the design requirements. The measured results verify the effectiveness of the feed chain design, which can be used in the next generation mobile communication satellite.

articleTitle: The Design of A Single-layer Broadband Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a simple new single-layer broadband metamaterial absorber is designed and analyzed. The surface layer is double notched wood comb type metal structure, the middle layer is F4B-2 dielectric substrate and the bottom layer is metal reflector. The thickness is 0.144λ. Through optimization, the absorption rate is over 90% in the frequency range of 7.68 GHz to 17.776 GHz, covering X and Ku bands. It produces relatively strong resonances at 8.3 GHz, 13.31 GHz and 16.35 GHz, achieving perfect absorption. The relative bandwidth is up to 79.32%. The metamaterial absorber has the advantages of simple structure, high absorption efficiency, wide bandwidth and small thickness.

articleTitle: Wideband Cavity-Backed Slot Subarray Fed by Gap Ridge Waveguide for 5G mmWave Base Station
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a bandwidth-improved cavity-backed unit cell slot subarray antenna fed by a gap ridge waveguide for Line-of-Sight (LoS) 5G mmWave applications. The proposed subarray is comprised of three layers. The top layer is the antenna layer in a 2 × 2 slots configuration, the cavity layer is in the middle and the ridge gap waveguide feeding is in the bottom layer. We propose to enhance the bandwidth of the unit cell subarray antenna by modifying the coupling slot in the cavity layer. The main advantage of the proposed method is that the bandwidth enhancement can be achieved without adding an extra tuning pin in the cavity layer, which eases mass production. The proposed structure is simulated with the CST software in an infinite array environment. The simulation results show that the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> is below -10 dB over 24 - 31.5 GHz frequency band covering a 27% bandwidth and the directivity is approximately 33.8 dBi when evaluated as a 16 × 16 element slot array. It is envisaged that the method can be advantageous for bandwidth enhancement of a practical cavity-backed slot array antenna.

articleTitle: A Study on Gain Enhancement of a Leaf-Shaped Bowtie Slot Antenna Array Employing Dielectric Superstrates
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a study on gain enhancement of a planar-type wideband linear array antenna through the use of dielectric superstrates with high dielectric constant. For the case where two-layered dielectric superstrates are placed above a leaf-shaped bowtie slot linear antenna array in E-plane, antenna characteristics are evaluated by the finite-difference time domain (FDTD) analysis. From the simulated results, it is confirmed that the gain is increased by around 4 dB in comparison with the case for the antenna array only, and that narrow-beam pattern is obtained in H-plane.

articleTitle: Metasurface Inspired Cavity Antenna with Improved Operation Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Metasurface inspired design as a valid solution for elevating the broadband performance of a cavity antenna operating at L and S bands is presented, by a comparison of antenna prototype without and with metasurface modulation. Two types of metasurface configurations labelled as A and B are introduced and embedded in a cavity aperture, which consists of several metallic stripes similar to the radiation dipole patches of antenna. The operation bandwidth for return loss less than -10 dB has been extended from 857 MHz for antenna prototype to 1090 and 1167 MHz after being modified with metasurfaces A and B, respectively. Simultaneously, the far field radiation patterns nearly keep the same, especially in the dominant radiation direction.

articleTitle: High Temporal Resolution Channel Emulation Utilizing Variable Delay and Polyphase Filters
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper proposes a method to emulate high temporal resolution wireless channel, using variable fractional delay filters. The design modifies tapped delay line model with Farrow structure. It features precise and variable delay without changing the filter coefficients. Furthermore, the integration with the ployphase filter structure makes it possible to apply in the emulation of wideband signals. The simulation results are discussed and analyzed, including the impact of the filter order and normalized bandwidth. Finally, the implement results based on this design are compared and summarized.

articleTitle: Aperture Distribution of RLSA for 5.8-GHz band Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Wireless power transmission system using two radial line slot arrays (RLSA) is proposed in this paper. The RLSAs are placed against each other in near-field region of the antenna. Two different array excitation types, uniform and rotation, are compared in terms of transmission distance and off-axis transmission loss.

articleTitle: A Novel F-shaped Hybrid Isolator Employed by Tx/Rx Antennas to Improve Antenna Performance
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel F-shaped hybrid isolator is proposed to reduce mutual coupling between two horizontally polarized X-band Tx/Rx microstrip antennas. The proposed configuration is composed of EBG-mushroom structure and two F-shaped metallic walls on both sides of EBG structure. The EBG-mushroom structure is designed for suppressing the surface wave propagation between the Tx/Rx antennas. The novelty of the F-shaped metal wall lies in its improvement of antenna radiation characteristics. The isolation level and radiation pattern performance of the Tx/Rx antennas with the hybrid isolator is simulated and compared to other isolation methods applied. The obtained result shows a maximum increase of 44.4dB in the isolation level, and main lobe direction is modified, comparing with original Tx/Rx antennas.

articleTitle: Direction Finding by Time-Modulated Array with Antenna Characteristic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of antenna performance in direction finding by Time-Modulated Array(TMA) is analyzed in terms of accuracy. By changing the directivity and main lobe direction of each receiving antenna, the accuracy of the direction finding is improved. As a result of the analysis through Root Mean Square Error(RMSE), the accuracy is improved to 70% compared with using isotropic antenna.

articleTitle: CSI Estimation by Beamforming and Blind Algorithm for WPT Terminal Stations
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The wireless power transfer (WPT) system is assumed with 5 GHz. However, there are wireless LAN (W-LAN) and dedicated short range communications (DSRC), and so on in this frequency band. If WPT terminals are used under this condition with the high power, the interference signals arrive to the other system such as W-LAN and DSRC even if the same frequency channels are not used. In this paper, the channel state information (CSI) estimation method from the other systems is proposed by using the multi-beam, blind algorithm, and successive interference cancellation. As a basic study, we assume that there are two other system terminals and show the effectiveness of the CSI estimation via a computer simulation using experimental measurement data.

articleTitle: Research on the Distribution Characteristics of Electromagnetic Environment in the Lightning Return Stroke Near-Field Area
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we simulate the lightning return stroke model and the return stroke physical process to study spatial and temporal distribution characteristics of electromagnetic fields near the lightning channel and ground (within the range of 100m from the lightning return stroke point) by using the transmission line (TL) engineering model and the three-dimensional electromagnetic field simulation software XFDTD based on finite difference time domain (FDTD) method. The distribution characteristics of electric field components emerge as the columnar and spherical. But the distributions of magnetic field components resemble cylinder.

articleTitle: Optomechanical Metamaterial/Metasurface and the Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the research achievements for the optomechanical metamaterials and metasurfaces in our group at the past several years. Firstly, the analysis for mechanical motion under the electromagnetic (EM) wave excitation of a metamaterial unit cell is developed, and the interaction between the EM wave and metamaterial unit cell is then provided both in air and liquid environments. Lastly, one of the potential applications for antenna power protection by using such kind of the optomechanical metasurface is proposed.

articleTitle: Parametric Scattering Center Modeling for the Complex Conducting Cavity
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The complex cavity is one of essentially structures of air vehicles, e.g., inlet duct and tail nozzle. Therefore, the scattered fields from the cavity are one of the most important scattering sources, which can be used to identify these kinds of structures. A scattering center (SC) modeling approach for complex cavities is introduced in this work, where geometrical optics (GO) with the full-wave numerical methods are used to obtain the locations and amplitudes of the SCs in the complex cavity. Two complex conducting cavities are investigated. The built models are validated through the comparisons between the simulated results by the models and those computed by full-wave numerical method. These results show that the models are of high precision in describing the signatures of cavities in the high resolution range profiles (HRRPs).

articleTitle: Development of a Numerical Smartphone Model for Evaluating Specific Absorption Rate in the Human Body
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, various electromagnetic (EM) applications have become common, and humans are frequently exposed to EM waves. Therefore, the effect of EM waves on the human body should be evaluated. In this study, we focused on the specific absorption rate (SAR) due to EM waves emitted from a smartphone, developed a numerical smartphone model, and confirmed its validity.

articleTitle: A Varactor-Based Frequency Reconfigurable Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel reconfigurable technique for dielectric resonator antenna by implementing frequency continuous adjustable bandpass filters is proposed in this paper. It is achieved by changing the total capacitance of the modified O-shaped filter with uniform impedance resonator via an integrated varactor within its structure. Moreover, the reconfigurable bandpass filter is incorporated within the offset microstrip feedline for the rectangular dielectric resonator antenna with wideband characteristic to form one resonant structure. The combination contributes to the operation frequency tuning for the antenna without multiple feeding paths or different excitation positions. The method makes the antenna has the filtering ability while preserve the good radiation performance. The simulated results have shown a frequency reconfigurable behavior, which is necessary for cognitive radio system and smart wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Design of Multimode Linear Array Antenna for the Interference Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multimode linear array antenna to maximize the number of the array elements for the interference mitigation by integrating a loop patch and a monopole antenna. The loop patch and the monopole antennas had maximum gains of 5.2 dBi and 1.6 dBi in the upper hemisphere pattern. The nulling performances are observed to demonstrate the interference mitigation, and the results shows a pattern null width of 13° and a null depth of 66.2 dB.

articleTitle: Analysis of Effective Coverage Area in 60GHz-Band Millimeter Wave Wireless LAN for High Speed Railway Passenger Car and Indoor Room
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Based on the transmission power and polarization, we conducted a basic research on how effectively the signal transmission coverage area can be expected even in the same 60 GHz band. We use the ray-tracing method to simulate two types of environment. One is high speed railway passenger car and other is indoor room.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Pulse Coupling Effects on a Crystalline Silicon Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Based on the weaking damage of the powerful electromagnetic pulse to soalr cells, the electromagnetic pulse coupling effects on a crystalline silicon solar cell is studied in this paper. First, a crystalline silicon solar cell is modeled in CST software. We simulate the model with three kinds of excitation signals and it is concluded that the resonance frequency is independent of the pulse form. Next, we compared with the measurement and the calculation results for surface current and the electric field intensity. Finally, the strongest resonance frequency is found by combining the impulse simulation results, and the selection scheme of testing frequency is put forward for engineering application.

articleTitle: Low RCS Path Antenna Array Based Units with Different Reflection Phase
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a low radar cross section (RCS) antenna array based on units with different reflection phase is proposed. The reflection phase of the antenna units can be controlled by the pin-diodes placed on the metal-ring around the radiation patch. However, the radiation performances of the units are similar while the pin-diodes are in different working states. By the chessboard arrangement of the sub-arrays, low RCS array is achieved for y-polarization wave incidence.

articleTitle: A Novel Triple-Mode Wideband Slotline Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel triple-mode planar wideband sloltine antenna is presented. The proposed antenna starts from a traditional slot one, which only has a radiation mode and suffers from intrinsic narrow bandwidth. To deal with this problem, two pairs of short-ended slots are symmetrically etched along the traditional slot one near the maximum electrical field of its full-wave radiation mode. After suitably choosing the locations and parameters of the short-ended slots, extra two radiation modes can be introduced and merged with the full-wave one, resulting in a wideband characteristic with three resonances. To validate this, a triple-mode prototype is designed and experimentally measured. The experimental results agree well with the theoretical analysis and simulated ones verifying a simple designing approach of wideband slotline antennas with three radiation modes.

articleTitle: Eight-Element Linear Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Array with Butler Matrix Feed Network for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An eight-element linear magneto-Electric dipole antenna array with Butler matrix feed network is presented for 5G Applications. The antenna arrays along with 8×8 Butler matrix as a beamforming network to obtain eight steerable beams, operating at 24.75-27.5GHz. Simulated results show that antenna array achieves a maximum gain of 14 dBi, and the eight beams cover the required 120° azimuth angle, of which the gains are greater than 9dBi.

articleTitle: Aperture-Integration Based Transient Diffraction Mechanism of Electromagnetic Scattering from Electrically Large Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the fundamental diffraction mechanism of transient electromagnetic (EM) scattering from an electrically large scatterer with relative smoothly varying surface curvatures based on time domain aperture integration (TD-AI) approaches. In this TD-AI technique, the transient responses are predicted by considering the effects of equal net time-delay in propagation when the incident wave propagates to the field point via EM scattering from the scatterer. The characteristics of the contributing contour, which is defined by the intersection of an equal time-delay curved aperture (ETDCA) and a time-varying equal path-length (TEPL) sphere, is employed to interpret the EM scattering mechanisms. numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the validity and feasibility of this general TD-AI technique.

articleTitle: 4G LTE Detection using NEMO Handy for PFSR Support System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: 4G is the fourth technology of broadband cellular network technology. In year 2016, 4G Long Term Evolution (LTE) has become one of the successful mobile wireless broadband technology and conduct a wide range of applications. Signal strength for 4G LTE is most important to maintain the data access demand used by various services. The demand for strong 4G LTE signal coverage for mobile services is increasing around the world. This paper presents a study on signal strength of 4G LTE network that focuses on Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP) and Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ) parameter that support the passive forward scattering radar (PFSR) system. In this study, Nemo Handy was used to detect signal strength, as well as support the result of human detection based on passive forward scattering radar system. Besides that, this study used a system called passive forward scattering radar that identifies any object that passes through between commercial transmitter and receiver that produces Doppler signature. For further study, this research was conducted at three different places, which are Dungun, Port Dickson and Taman Suria using 1.8GHz LTE frequency. Then, the data received by the receiver was collected and analysed by using MATLAB software. Conclusively, this detection of strong and poor signal cellular network may help telecommunication companies in Malaysia to provide better cellular network service.

articleTitle: Dual-band Omnidirectional Antenna for WiFi Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a dual-band omnidirectional patch antenna with stable ellipticity of less than 1.8dB is introduced. This antenna is designed for the WiFi application operations at 2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz. It has an advantage of a much smaller and simpler structure compared with traditional dual-band WiFi antennas. Details of design, simulated results of this dual-band omnidirectional antenna are presented and discussed. The results confirm the validity of this design, which meet the requirement of WiFi application.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Compensation using Defected Ground Structure for Low-band LTE Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a mutual coupling reduction technique for multiple antennas designed on small chassis is investigated. This technique is based on introducing a meander-shaped defected ground structure (DGS) unit cell located on the top edge in between two planar inverted-F antennas (PIFAs). It functions as a filter to improve the isolation between antennas, which are designed to operate in the low-band Long-Term Evolution (LTE), 698-960 MHz, centered at 829 MHz. At this frequency, the insertion loss (S21) is seen to be improved to -26 dB. To proof the improvement of this technique, the antennas and DGS have been simulated and measured, and compared with another conventional design without the DGS. Simulation results indicated that the mutual coupling is reduced from -3 dB to -13 dB, whereas the reflection coefficient is improved from -16 dB to -19 dB. Meanwhile, measurements also indicated an improved mutual coupling of -7 dB with the use of the proposed DGS structure.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarization Beam Scanning Antenna Array Based on TE01/TE10 Modes
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 30 GHz substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) dual-linear polarization antenna excited by TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>/TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> modes is presented. The antenna is polarized horizontally in TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode and vertically in TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> mode. In addition, because the width of this antenna is only 0.5λ, it's possible to design a dual-linear polarization beam scanning antenna array.

articleTitle: Automatic Calibration Switch Array of Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A twenty-four channel switch for phased array antenna calibration is proposed in this paper. The operating frequency range of the switch is below 3GHz. A host computer is designed to control the selection of the switching channel. The measured results show that insertion loss of the switch is low and isolation of the switch is high, which are approximately -2dB and generally less than -20dB at 2.7GHz, respectively. The switch is designed to simplify the calibration process of phased array antenna, which has important application value and practical significance for the calibration work of phased array antenna.

articleTitle: Three Ways to Decouple Multiple Antennas in A Mobile Terminal
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces three antenna decoupling methods named MIMO multi-feed antenna, Single parasitic dual frequency antenna and Meta-Surface Antenna Array Decoupling (MAAD). They are respectively an eight MIMO multi-feed antenna system, which operating in the 5G wireless and sub 6 GHZ. Single parasitic dual frequency antenna, introduce a dual-frequency parasitic antenna element between the two antennas. Meta-surface antenna array, place a suspended meta-surface composed periodic square split ring resonators (SRRs) on the antenna array. These methods can significantly application scenarios in both mobile terminals and MIMO base stations of 5G wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized 6:1 Unequal Wilkinson Power Divider Based on Plasmonic Waveguides Loaded with Inductors
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel miniaturized 6:1 unequal Wilkinson power divider is proposed using spoof surface plasmon polariton (SPP) waveguide loaded with inductors. Compared with conventional Wilkinson power divider, the proposed SPP divider can realize high distribution ratio of 6:1 with excellent performance. Here, the SPP waveguides are combined with the unequal Wilkinson power divider. Meanwhile, due to the slow-wave property of the SPP waveguide, the miniaturization of the power divider can be achieved. At the central frequency, the return loss S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and port isolation S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">32</inf> are both lower than -19dB, while power difference between two output ports is 7.68dB. The size of the novel power divider is 45% less than that of conventional Wilkinson power divider.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Patch Antenna with High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-polarized patch antenna with high isolation. The proposed antenna can have a high degree of isolation with the return loss substantially unchanged by introducing a microstrip transmission line network. The |S11| of antenna is less than -10 dB from 3.28 GHz to 3.76 GHz, and its |S21| is less than -25 dB from 3.01 GHz to 3.70 GHz. Finally, it is found that the cross polarization of the proposed antenna is also better than that of the initial antenna by comparing the radiation [patterns of the two antennas.

articleTitle: The Antenna Measurements using the Three-antenna Extrapolation Range
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Based on the extrapolation range facility, which was built in National Institute of Metrology (NIM) China, several antenna measurement methods are investigated, including the three-antenna extrapolation method, the commonly used gain-transfer method and the novel reference-antenna method by combining the extrapolation technique. The uncertainties for the measurement results using these methods are investigated. It is demonstrated that by using the extrapolation technique, a reference gain standard with high degree of accuracy is obtained, and it will help reducing the gain uncertainty in other antenna measurement ranges by employing it in the gain-transfer method.

articleTitle: An X-band Slice Receiving Module for AESA
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An X-band receiving module has been developed to support active electronically steerable antenna. The module is composed of a single RF receiving channel, which has the functions of power modulation, phase shift and attenuation. In order to meet the requirement of small size, high maintainability, a new vertical interconnection technology is proposed by using two blind-mate RF connectors, and a custom miniature DC/control 15-pin blind-mate connector, and the multi-functional chip (MFC) technique and multi-chip module (MCM) technique are also adopted. The channel gain of the receiving module is more than 31dB, the noise figure is less than 2.2dB, the amplitude error is less than 0.2dB (RMS), the phase error is less than 2 degree (RMS), the size of the module is 40mm*20mm*11mm and the total power consumption is less than 0.5W. The methodology and concept was proved by successful production and fully testing of 600 modules.

articleTitle: Glide symmetries and their application for electromagnetic periodic structures
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we summarize the latest discoveries on glide symmetry for electromagnetic devices. Glide symmetries have demonstrated the ability to improve the response of conventional periodic structures. In particular, they have been proposed to increase the bandwidth and isotropy of unit cells, which can be used for lenses. Additionally, glide symmetry has been used to increase the bandwidth of electromagnetic band gaps, which can be used to produce filters, flange interconnections and gap waveguide technology. Recently, glide symmetries have also been proposed for reducing the size of Luneburg lenses based on transformation optics. In this specific case, unit cells possessing glide symmetry provide a broadband anisotropic response. Finally, glide symmetry has been employed to improve the radiation control in leaky-wave antennas and to reduce their cost of manufacturing. Due to the numerous examples of the virtues of glide symmetries for electromagnetic purposes, the number of investigations on the topic is increasing every year and new discoveries are continuously arising.

articleTitle: All-Electronic Terahertz Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An all-electronic terahertz (THz) imaging system has been developed to image objects in submillimeter-scale resolution. Its high range resolution is achieved through the use of the broadband sweep signal, whose frequency ranges from 325 to 500 GHz, and the synthetic aperture technique is applied to improve two-dimensional cross-range resolution. High-resolution threedimensional THz images can be obtained using the range migration algorithm after the measurement calibration. The system design is presented and the imaging resolution is verified by the experimental results of standard test chart.

articleTitle: Tunable electromagnetically induced transparency via graphene in microwave band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The phenomenon of electromagnetic induced transparency (EIT) based on graphene in microwave band has seldom been studied due to its shortcomings in frequency modulation in this band. However, based on the excellent tunability of graphene, EIT with adjustable amplitude in microwave frequency band is still applicable. In this letter, a tunable EIT structure based on graphene in microwave band has been proposed, which has a transparent window at 1.6 GHz with a tunable transparency from about 40% to 85% adjusting the sheet resistance of graphene. The result shows that, the proposed structure has excellent adjustability and switching characteristics.

articleTitle: A Microstrip Leaky Wave Antenna For Frequency Sensitivity Enhancement With Flat Gain
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a microstrip leaky wave antenna (MLWA) based on the composite right/left-handed structure for the frequency sensitivity enhancement with a flat gain. Different from the conventional ones, the microstrip meander lines are introduced to increase the slope of effective phase constant versus frequency of LWAs and, hence, the beam scanning range. Finally, the antenna prototype with 16 unit cells exhibits the simulated beam scanning angle of -46° to 48° over the frequency range from 10.3 to 11.5 GHz with a gain variation of less than 2.0 dBi.

articleTitle: A Compact Broadband 16×16 Butler Matrix for Multibeam Antenna Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact 16×16 Butler Matrix operated from 9 GHz - 11 GHz. Compared with the traditional structure, the presented network is much simpler and can be easily designed. The number of needed components in the design is only sixty, where the number of crossovers is four. In addition, the designed network can be fully realized in a single layer laminate with the size of 165 mm × 165 mm (5.5λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 5.5λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>). It is shown that the maximum simulated output phase error at 10 GHz is only ±8° and the transmission coefficients are in the range of -14.5 ± 1.5dB over the bandwidth. The measured and simulated results agree well. The designed network can be a potential candidate for the one or two dimensional multibeam array antennas.

articleTitle: Improvement of Channel Capacity using Relay for Polarized MIMO Transmission
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Polarized MIMO transmission is one of the key technology for realizing terrestrial 4K and 8K broadcasts. In this paper, the improvement effect of channel capacity by MIMO transmission using relay is evaluated. As a result of numerical study, channel capacity is improved by relay in residential area.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized Patch Antenna Array with Metasurface for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-polarized patch antenna with metasurface is proposed for base station application, the bandwidth for VSWR<; 2 and VSWR<; 1.5 of the 1×3 array is 3.35-3.94GHz and 3.42-3.74GHz respectively. The isolation is over 25dB, and the half power beamwidth (HPBW) is 65° in horizontal and 29° in vertical. In the operating band, the good performance of impedance matching, high isolation and stable radiation pattern can be achieved.

articleTitle: Modal Analysis for Gap Waveguide Considering Structural Periodicity in Propagation Direction
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a modal analysis for gap waveguide by considering the structural periodicity in the propagation direction. We firstly analyze the Floquet modes and the generalized scattering matrix (GSM) expressed by eigenmodes for the cross-section with the metal pins. The GSM based on the modes for the cross section is converted to a GSM based on the Floquet modes. While the GSM based on the modes for the cross section has several propagation modes, the GSM based on the Floquet modes has a single propagation mode in the stopband by EBG structure. The GSM based on the Floquet modes is suitable to understand propagation of gap waveguide circuits.

articleTitle: Measurement of Human Body Blockage in HAPS Communications with Consideration of Elevation Angle
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A High-Altitude Platform Station (HAPS), which provides communications services from an altitude of 20 km via an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) such as a balloon, airship, or other aircraft, is attracting much attention as a new mobile communications platform for an ultra-wide coverage area and disaster-resilient networks. A HAPS can provide mobile communications services directly to smartphones, which are commonly used in terrestrial mobile communications networks with Fourth Generation Long Term Evolution (4G LTE), and in the near future, Fifth Generation New Radio (5G NR). In order to design efficient cell configurations for mobile communications in HAPS, we need a radio wave propagation model that takes into consideration the terrain, vegetation, urban areas, suburban areas, building entry loss, etc. Also to offer mobile communications services directly to smartphones, human body blockage characteristics with high elevation angles is required. In this paper, we use a human phantom to measure the human body blockage characteristics at high elevation angles and clarify human body blockage loss on line of sight links. Further we also consider the human body blockage loss in non-line of sight links.

articleTitle: Multi-Frequency Millimeter-Wave Large-Scale Channel Characteristics in Suburban Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The measurement-based large-scale channel characterizations in suburban environment across 28 GHz and 39 GHz are presented. Using a flexible millimeter channel sounder, sufficient measurement data have been collected for large-scale channel characteristics in both line-of-sight (LoS) and obstacleLoS (OLoS) scenarios. Both closed-in and floating-intercept path loss models are respectively employed to analyze the effects of frequency and foliage blockage on large-scale fading for directional and omnidirectional channels, indicating the impact of foliage blockage on the mmWave propagation in suburban environments.

articleTitle: A Mixed-form Nested Equivalence Source Approximation Method with Adaptive Group Size
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a mixed-form nested equivalence source approximation method with adaptive group size octree is proposed for multiscale problems. The mixed "skeleton" and "equivalence" nested approximation is introduced to compress the impedance matrix of the method of moments (MoM) for the wideband multiscale simulations. For the multiscale problems with non-uniform mesh, an adaptive group is employed to get a uniform number of unknowns at leaf level. Numerical results show our proposed method is with O(NlogN) computational complexity for both time and memory requirements, N is the number of unknowns. Multiscale simulations demonstrate the validity of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Thin Transmitarray Panel with full 360-degree Phase Shift Range
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a new design technique to reduce the thickness of the transmitarray (TA) panel while maintaining 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> phase shift range. Two types of unit cells, the receive-transmit unit cell and the frequency selective surface (FSS) unit cell, are placed in the same aperture. Comparing to the existing ultra-thin TA designs of similar panel thickness, the presented TAs do not suffer from the phase quantization loss and achieve better aperture efficiency. This study proves that it is viable to mix different types of TA unit cells to design a TA. The developed TA shows better gain than a homogeneous TA using the same elements and improved the overall efficiency by 60%. To verify the design concept, one TA with central frequency at 13.3 GHz was designed, fabricated and measured. The measured gain is 21.3 dBi and the calculated aperture efficiency of the TA is 37.9%.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Class F Inverse Power Amplifier for S-Band Telemetry Sub-System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a high power, high efficiency power amplifier using GaN HEMT class F inverse with harmonic termination network at operating frequency 2.14GHZ. The optimum impedances for input and output 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>,2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>, and 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> harmonics were extracted using load and source pull analysis. Effect of with and without harmonic termination on the performance of class F inverse power amplifier is evaluated by its output power, PAE and gate stress. Propose class F inverse amplifier is fabricated on RO4350B. Measured results indicate that class F inverse power amplifier has achieved high output power 36.3dBm with high efficiency of 71%.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Capacitively Coupled Microstrip Patch Array Antenna for 79 GHz Radar Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel capacitively coupled microstrip patch array antenna is proposed for 79 GHz radar sensors. The proposed antenna has advantages of low profile, low cost and ease of fabrication by implementing it on a millimeter- wave substrate. Two types of capacitively coupled patch arrays are designed and developed; one is 1 × 18 array for the short- range radar (SRR) sensor and the other is 4 × 18 array for the mid-range radar (MRR) sensor. To confirm the feasibility of the proposed antenna, the prototypes of the designed antennas are fabricated and measured. The simulated and measured reflection coefficients are in good agreement and less than -10 dB in a wide range of frequencies including 79 GHz. The measured maximum antenna gains are 13.94 dBi and 18.03 dBi for the 1 × 18 array and 4 × 18 array in the boresight direction at 79 GHz.

articleTitle: X-band Slotted Waveguide Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A planar slot array antenna of 12x16 elements is designed at X-band with uniform aperture distribution to get maximum aperture efficiency. The antenna is centre fed from iris coupling slot with alternate slot inclinations to feed the radiating waveguides in phase. A feeding network of nonstandard waveguides is formed to couple the power from feeding network to radiating aperture. A radiating aperture also of non-standard size is selected to give the low profile antenna at 9.65GHz. The longitudinal shunt slots are used with alternate offsets directions to radiate in phase at boresight.

articleTitle: Design of an Implantable Antenna for Wireless Communication of Ingestible Capsule Endoscope
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a design for an implantable antenna operating in the Medical Device Radio communications Service (MedRadio) (401-406 MHz) band for wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE). Simulation results show the proposed antenna has good performance in terms of return loss, a bandwidth of 310 MHz to 580 MHz and a maximum realised gain of -31.3 dB. The simulated radiation pattern of this antenna is omnidirectional. The tolerance of the antenna owing to bending and different capsule shell thicknesses is also investigated and indicates that the proposed antenna is an excellent candidate for WCE applications.

articleTitle: Multi-focus Hologram with Fabry-Perot Antenna Based on Coding Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, A Fabry-Perot (FP) cavity antenna based on coding metasurface is addressed to realize a four-point focused hologram. A three-layer partial reflection surface (PRS) unit is designed by fixing the reflective phase to generate plane wave and arranging the transmission phase combined with the weight Gerchberg-Saxton (GSW) holographic algorithm to accomplish multi-focus. Four symmetrical focus points are perfectly observed in theory calculation and simulation with the location (±1.3λ, ±1.3λ, 2.5λ) at 27.5GHz operating frequency. This work can be extended for more complex hologram construction and 2-D beam steering applications in the future.

articleTitle: Low-loss, Wideband 3dB Hybrid Coupler Based on AMC for 5G Millimeter-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A a low-loss, wideband 3 dB hybrid coupler with novel artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) packaging based on the principle of branch-line coupler structure is presented for 5G millimeter-wave communication application. The AMC structure is employed to suppress the spurious radiation.The prototype of the novel design has been fabricated and simulated. The result shows that the proposed hybrid coupler has magnitude differences between the through and coupled port less than 0.25 dB over the frequency range from 27 to 33 GHz. The phase differences between the through and coupled ports are 90± 2.5°.

articleTitle: A Novel Low Cost System for Measuring Complex Permittivity of Dielectric Materials
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low-cost system for measuring the complex permittivity is presented in this paper. The system is comprised of a coaxial-waveguide transmitter, four segments of empty waveguide (EW) and a shorting terminal. This simple system can determine the permittivity and conductivity of the sample material under test by using a conventional Vector Network Analyzer(VNA). The underlying principle of the measurement technique are presented followed by some simulation and experimental results for a fabricated system, that serve to verify the validity and efficacy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improvement of a Circular Polarized Patch Antenna using a Split Ring Resonators-Based Radome
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A radome based on the split ring resonator (SRR) to improve the performance of a circular microstrip antenna is proposed in this work. The radome is located 10 mm over the circular-polarized antenna designed to operate between 5.2 GHz and 6.4 GHz. The radome consists of a 4 x 5 array of SRR unit cells, with each unit cell designed using a pair of SRR located adjacent to each other. A circular microstrip antenna was then designed to evaluate the radome, indicating improved performance. Simulations indicated circular polarization of the proposed antenna with gain improvement from 4 GHz to 5.14 GHz, with an axial ratio of 1.4 dB in the presence of the SRR radome. In comparison, the axial ratio of the antenna is 14.87 dB without the SRR radome.

articleTitle: Graphene-loaded THz Frequency Selective Surface with Tunable Transmission Band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a graphene-loaded bandwidth tunable frequency-selective surface (TFSS) working in THz spectrum from 0.3THz to 0.9THz, the pass bandwidth has great changed when bias voltage varies on the graphene. When the added chemical potential is becoming larger, the insertion loss of TFSS is getting smaller, the transmission bandwidth characteristics becomes wider. The maximum transmittance coefficient is up to -0.9dB.

articleTitle: W-band Free-space Planar Offset Short
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Electrical properties of materials are requisite to design electromagnetic (EM) device and system. Free-space material measurement method that measures free-space scattering parameter of MUT (Material Under Test) located at the middle of two antennas is suitable for non-destructively testing the MUT without prior machining and physical contact in high frequencies. In this paper, a planar offset short is proposed as a free-space planar reflection standard because the phase of the reflection coefficient of the planar offset short is proportional to the offset of the short. Fabrication of a planar offset short is described and its measurement result is shown in W-band (75-110 GHz).

articleTitle: Study toward multi-beam patterns suitable for multi-beam massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Multi-beam massive MIMO configuration has been proposed that utilizes the beam selection with high power in an analog part and blind algorithm with independent component analysis (ICA) which does not need channel state information (CSI) in a digital part. However, its performance depends on the beam pattern of the multi-beams, and there might be optimal multi-beam patterns. In this paper, we propose a method to determine the multi-beam patterns suitable for the proposed massive MIMO system, and clarify the performance by the difference of multi-beam patterns.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in EM Parametric Modeling Using Combined Neural Network and Transfer Function
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of the recent advances in electromagnetic (EM) modeling approaches using combined neural network and transfer function (neuro-transfer function or neuro-TF) and its application to antenna design. In this technique, neural networks are trained to learn the relationship between pole/residues of the transfer functions and geometrical parameters. After the modeling process, the trained model can be used to provide accurate and fast prediction of the EM behavior with geometrical parameters as variables. This technique is illustrated by a example of EM parametric modeling of an ultra-wideband antenna.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Phased Array using Sequential Rotated Technique for Ku-band Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a stripline fed circularly polarized (CP) phased array with sequential rotated technology is proposed for satellite applications in Ku-band. The antenna element is designed based on multilayer PCB process. It is composed of SIW cavity, aperture coupling slot, hollow cavity, and stacked patches. CP operation is realized by truncated corner. The array presents the advantages of light weight, low profile and wide scan performance. The design has been constructed with a 8×8 (64 element) array. Results show that the array achieves stable gain when scanning up to ±60°in all azimuth planes, and the 3-dB axial ratio (AR) in the mainlobe region is lower than 3 dB when scanning. Numerical Results of full-wave simulation by virtue of HFSS demonstrate the design.

articleTitle: Design of a 35 GHz Circularly Polarized Rectenna for Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A circularly polarized rectenna based on slot coupled microstrip antenna is designed at 35GHz. For the antenna part, circular polarization can be obtained by cutting the opposite corner of the radiation patch. Meanwhile, good impendence performance can be achieved by feeding the antenna through slot coupled microstrip. For the rectifying circuit part, it can convert the received RF signals into DC singles. By designing reasonable matching circuit and output DC-pass filter, good RF-to-DC conversion efficiency can be obtained. The simulated results show that the axial-ratio (AR) of the presented rectanna is 0.4dB and the gain is 6.25dBic at 35GHz. When the input power is 20dBm and the load impendence is 139 Ω, the maximum conversion efficiency values of 61% is achieved. Therefore, this rectenna can be applied to wireless power transmission.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Profile Antenna Considering the Thermal Properties
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact and low profile antenna for aerocraft is presented in the paper. For the aerocraft application, not only the electrical properties but also the thermal properties should be considered in the antenna design. Full metal structure is used in the antenna design to meet the thermal requirement. C-shaped structure and shorting pins are used in the antenna design for the compact and low profile antenna design, which can reduce the antenna environment temperature because small size means the small wind resistance. The size of the antenna is only 0.19×0.09× 0.06 λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, where λ is the center frequency.

articleTitle: Complementary Magneto-Electric Coupling Feeding Methods for Low-Profile High-Isolation Dual-Polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low profile dual polarized circular microstrip patch antenna (CMPA) with high isolation and low polarization levels is proposed using complementary magneto-electric coupling feeding methods. For Port-1, electromagnetic energy is coupled to the radiating patch through a slot etched on the ground plane, which is known as magnetic coupling. The CMPA radiates a y-polarization wave. For Port-2, electromagnetic energy is directly coupled to the radiating patch from a forked microstrip line, which is electric coupling. The CMPA radiates a x-polarization wave. The magnetic coupling and electric coupling are complementary. In the whole frequency band, the isolation between these two ports are higher than 55 dB without any decoupling design. The cross polarization levels are less than -42 dB in E-plane and -30 dB in H-plane for each port. And also, the profile is only 0.02 λ0. The complementary feeding methods could be a good candidate to design a high-isolation dual polarized MPA without any complicated decoupling network.

articleTitle: Study of Extremely Low Frequency Electromagnetic Wave Propagation along the Seashore of Bajiaogang in Shandong, China
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Great attention has been paid to the extremely low frequency (ELF) electromagnetic waves due to its important application in long-distance communication, undersea detection and guidance. Most previous researches, however, focus on the propagation characteristics of VLF/ELF signal conducted by earth-ionosphere or undersea water. This paper endeavors to study the ELF wave propagation travellin along the seashore. To achieve this, an experiment is designed: high sensitive conducted magnetometers are adopted to capture the ELF signal produced by a pair of electrodes submerged in the sea-water along the coast. The results showed that for 5 Hz and 10 Hz the trend agreed with the normal logarithm function, but with a pecularity of peak at around 550 m.
